Messages.Author: James Hamblin
Messages.Body:
Tono wrote:
>
> Can you play two Out-of-Turns in the same turn???

No. By playing an Out-of-Turn master, you are using your next turn's
master phase early, which is why you don't get to play a master in that
next turn. But, since you have used it up, you can't play another
Out-of-Turn until after your next turn.

James

Messages.Author: James Hamblin
Messages.Body:
> Excuse me? I do not recall reading anything like this in the rules.
> Could you tell me where I can read it to verify?

V:tES rulebook, page 10:

Out-of-Turn: Out-of-turn cards can only be played when it is not your
turn. If you play this type of card, you lose your master phase action
during the master phase of your next turn. Once you've played an
out-of-turn master card, you can't play another one until after your
next turn.

That's the literal rules. It seems to me that Anson/Rumors would let
you play another OOT before your next turn, but I may be wrong. Shawn?



No because you are allowed only one master per turn.
Playing a master Out of Turn is like anticipate your next master phase.
If you have Anson or whatever card that allows you to play more than one
master in a turn so you can play as many Out of Turn as the number of
master you
can play. You can also mix Out of Turn and Master : playing one Sudden and,

Hmm. This is a direct contradiction of a Wylie (which I thought went up
to the rules team) which says that using an OOT burns your entire Master
Phase, and that no Master Phase actions at all (chantry, etc) work
thereafter.

And that's why. NOt that I object to the ruling changing, but these two
elements are directly contradictory.

>to the rules team) which says that using an OOT burns your entire Master
>Phase, and that no Master Phase actions at all (chantry, etc) work
>thereafter.

Mr. Wylie was giving the (then current) Jyhad ruling. With VtES, WotC
introduced the "master phase action" and changed the rule on MOoT cards
so that playing a MOoT would only burn your next MastertPhaseAction (MPA),
not the entire phase.

Mr. Wylie pointed out the change when it occurred.

>: Important note: remember that, according to the rules, you can only play
>: one OOT until after your next turn.

>And that's why. NOt that I object to the ruling changing, but these two
>elements are directly contradictory.

The new rules also explicitly deny the possibility of playing more than
one MOoT between your turns (as an obstacle to using the new MPA rules
to implement some degenerate MOoT combo).



> thereafter.

I checked with Tom, and after some discussion:

IT'S A REVERSAL!

The official ruling is now that you get the Anson master action if you
use Sudden Reversal before your master phase.

To me it doesn't make any sense that you lose the master phase because
you play one master card. One master card equals the expenditure of one
master action.
